question.:question/problem: Evaluate the integral $\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(3)}}5xe^{x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's introduce the new variable $u=x^{2}.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=2x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{d}u=x\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

Next, we determine the new limits of integration:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{\ln(3)}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\ln(3)$ |

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(3)}}5xe^{x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(3)}}5e^{x^{2}}\cdot x\,\mathrm{d}x \\ & = \int_{0}^{\ln(3)}5e^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = \frac{5}{2}\int_{0}^{\ln(3)}e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = \frac{5}{2}e^{u}\big|_{0}^{\ln(3)} \\ & = \frac{5}{2}(e^{\ln(3)}-e^{0}) \\ & = \frac{5}{2}(3-1) \\ & = \frac{5}{2}(2) \\ & = 5.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Next, we determine the new limits of integration:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{\ln(5)}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $2\ln(5)$ |

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(5)}}\frac{1}{5}xe^{2x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \frac{1}{5}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(5)}}e^{2x^{2}}\cdot x\,\mathrm{d}x \\ & = \frac{1}{5}\int_{0}^{2\ln(5)}e^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = \frac{1}{20}\int_{0}^{2\ln(5)}e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = \frac{1}{20}e^{u}\big|_{0}^{2\ln(5)} \\ & = \frac{1}{20}(e^{2\ln(5)}-e^{0}) \\ & = \frac{1}{20}(25-1) \\ & = \frac{24}{20} \\ & = \frac{6}{5}.\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem: Evaluate the integral $\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(7)}}6xe^{x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's introduce the new variable $u=x^{2}.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=2x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{d}u=x\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

Next, we determine the new limits of integration:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{\ln(7)}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\ln(7)$ |

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(7)}}6xe^{x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(7)}}6e^{x^{2}}\cdot x\,\mathrm{d}x \\ & = \int_{0}^{\ln(7)}6e^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = 3\int_{0}^{\ln(7)}e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = 3e^{u}\big|_{0}^{\ln(7)} \\ & = 3(e^{\ln(7)}-e^{0}) \\ & = 3(7-1) \\ & = 3(6) \\ & = 18.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce the new variable $u=2x^{2}.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u=x\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

Next, we determine the new limits of integration:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{\ln(3)}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $2\ln(3)$ |

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(3)}}\frac{1}{4}xe^{2x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \frac{1}{4}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(3)}}e^{2x^{2}}\cdot x\,\mathrm{d}x \\ & = \frac{1}{4}\int_{0}^{2\ln(3)}e^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = \frac{1}{16}\int_{0}^{2\ln(3)}e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = \frac{1}{16}e^{u}\big|_{0}^{2\ln(3)} \\ & = \frac{1}{16}(e^{2\ln(3)}-e^{0}) \\ & = \frac{1}{16}(9-1) \\ & = \frac{8}{16} \\ & = \frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate the integral $\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(6)}}\frac{1}{8}xe^{2x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's introduce the new variable $u=2x^{2}.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u=x\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

Next, we determine the new limits of integration:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{\ln(6)}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $2\ln(6)$ |

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(6)}}\frac{1}{8}xe^{2x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \frac{1}{8}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(6)}}e^{2x^{2}}\cdot x\,\mathrm{d}x \\ & = \frac{1}{8}\int_{0}^{2\ln(6)}e^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = \frac{1}{32}\int_{0}^{2\ln(6)}e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = \frac{1}{32}e^{u}\big|_{0}^{2\ln(6)} \\ & = \frac{1}{32}(e^{2\ln(6)}-e^{0}) \\ & = \frac{1}{32}(36-1) \\ & = \frac{35}{32} \\ & = \frac{35}{32}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate the integral $\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(2)}}\frac{1}{6}xe^{2x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's introduce the new variable $u=2x^{2}.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u=x\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

Next, we determine the new limits of integration:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{\ln(2)}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $2\ln(2)$ |

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(2)}}\frac{1}{6}xe^{2x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \frac{1}{6}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln(2)}}e^{2x^{2}}\cdot x\,\mathrm{d}x \\ & = \frac{1}{6}\int_{0}^{2\ln(2)}e^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = \frac{1}{24}\int_{0}^{2\ln(2)}e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = \frac{1}{24}e^{u}\big|_{0}^{2\ln(2)} \\ & = \frac{1}{24}(e^{2\ln(2)}-e^{0}) \\ & = \frac{1}{24}(4-1) \\ & = \frac{3}{24} \\ & = \frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
